infanticide_ban.name: Infant Killing Outlawed
infanticide_ban.observation: Killing a newborn is punished as murder, and a father may no longer decide at the hearth whether a child will live.

fifteen_year_assessment.name: Fifteen-Year Assessment
fifteen_year_assessment.observation: Heads and land are assessed afresh every fifteen years, and the tax follows the new count.

town_to_estate_drift.name: Flight to the Estates
town_to_estate_drift.observation: As the towns shrink, their people drift to estates and hill villages; fewer die of town fevers, and fewer trades are practised.
town_to_estate_drift.social_consequence: Townsfolk become the lord's tenants, and the old town walls enclose gardens and ruins.

settler_estate_shares.name: Settler Estate Shares
settler_estate_shares.observation: Settling peoples receive a set share of the host landowners' estates, a third of the land or the slaves, by treaty.
settler_estate_shares.social_consequence: Old landowners resent the strangers quartered on their land by law.

foundling_free_status.name: Foundlings Stay Free
foundling_free_status.observation: A child exposed and taken up by a stranger is free, not the finder's slave, and more are taken up.

refuge_site_towns.name: Refuge Towns
refuge_site_towns.observation: Refugees from the plains build towns on hilltops and lagoon islands where raiders cannot reach them, crowded and short of clean water.

conqueror_landed_settlement.name: Conquerors Settled on the Land
conqueror_landed_settlement.observation: The conquering host is settled on the land it took, each warrior with his holding and his duty to ride when called.
conqueror_landed_settlement.ability_reason: Conquest becomes a standing order that can hold its gains, with a warrior class rooted on the land.
conqueror_landed_settlement.social_consequence: The natives till for new masters of another tongue, and the two peoples live apart for generations.

bride_dower_gift.name: Bride's Dower
bride_dower_gift.observation: The groom secures a morning gift and a dower to the bride, hers to keep if she is widowed.

child_oblation.name: Child Oblation
child_oblation.observation: Families give a young child to a religious house to be raised and trained, and it seldom leaves.
child_oblation.social_consequence: Religious houses fill with the younger sons and daughters of the realm, who never marry.

presumed_death_term.name: Presumed Death
presumed_death_term.observation: A wife whose husband has been gone a set term of years may treat him as dead and marry again.

captive_artisan_resettlement.name: Captive Craftsmen
captive_artisan_resettlement.observation: Craftsmen taken in war are marched home and settled in the ruler's cities to work for him.
captive_artisan_resettlement.social_consequence: Whole quarters of captive strangers work under guard, bringing their skills and their fevers with them.

intermarriage_permission.name: Intermarriage Permitted
intermarriage_permission.observation: Settlers may lawfully marry native women and men, and the children inherit from both.

ranked_clan_genealogies.name: Ranked Clan Genealogies
ranked_clan_genealogies.observation: The pedigrees of the great clans are ranked and written, and birth decides who may hold which office.
ranked_clan_genealogies.ability_reason: Office and marriage now follow a written ranking of lineages that the court can consult and enforce.
ranked_clan_genealogies.social_consequence: Able men of low lineage find every door shut, and a genealogist's roll now says who belongs at court.

blood_heir_rule.name: Heirs of the Body
blood_heir_rule.observation: Only heirs of the body may inherit; adoption falls out of use, and a childless line ends with its holder.

soldier_farmer_holdings.name: Soldier-Farmer Holdings
soldier_farmer_holdings.observation: Families hold frontier land for as long as they send a son to serve, generation after generation.

godparent_kinship.name: Godparent Kinship
godparent_kinship.observation: Sponsors at a child's naming become kin to its parents, and the bond ties families across villages.

herder_tribute_registers.name: Herder Tribute Registers
herder_tribute_registers.observation: Herding families who settle are written into registers as tribute households under their own chiefs.

wide_kin_marriage_ban.name: Wide Kin Marriage Ban
wide_kin_marriage_ban.observation: Marriage is forbidden to cousins out to distant degrees, and brides must be sought in other villages.

child_fosterage.name: Fosterage
child_fosterage.observation: Children are sent to be raised by kin or a patron, and grow up bound to two households.

frontier_repopulation.name: Frontier Repopulation
frontier_repopulation.observation: Whole districts are moved by order to repopulate an emptied frontier, and many die on the road.
frontier_repopulation.social_consequence: Uprooted families remember the order that moved them, and the new frontier is full of strangers.

foundling_house.name: Foundling House
foundling_house.observation: A house takes in abandoned infants, with wet-nurses and a warden, and records each child it receives.
foundling_house.ability_reason: A child left at the gate now has a chance it never had on the roadside.
foundling_house.social_consequence: Many still die inside; the house becomes a place where the poor can leave a child they cannot feed without shame.

commemorative_death_books.name: Books of the Dead
commemorative_death_books.observation: Religious houses keep books of the dead to be remembered at their yearly services, name by name.

hearth_tax_counts.name: Hearth Counts
hearth_tax_counts.observation: Households are counted by their hearths for the tax, and families crowd round one fire to pay less.

hereditary_unfree_status.name: Unfree Birth
hereditary_unfree_status.observation: A child with one unfree parent is born unfree and belongs to the lord's roll.
hereditary_unfree_status.social_consequence: A free man who marries an unfree woman sees his children born into bondage, and the lord's roll of bondfolk grows each generation.

invited_craft_colonies.name: Invited Craftsmen
invited_craft_colonies.observation: Foreign craftsmen are invited to settle with privileges, a quarter of their own and freedom from some dues.

childhood_disease_book.name: Children's Diseases
childhood_disease_book.observation: A physician writes the first book on the diseases of children, from teething to the fevers of the young.

fortified_frontier_villages.name: Chartered Frontier Villages
fortified_frontier_villages.observation: Free farmers settle fortified frontier villages under charters that fix their dues and rights.

marriage_out_fee.name: Marriage-Out Fee
marriage_out_fee.observation: A tenant's daughter who marries off the estate owes the lord a fee for the loss of her and her children.

herder_sedentarization.name: Herders Settle
herder_sedentarization.observation: Herding peoples settle as farming villages near the towns and trade their flocks for fields.

village_nucleation.name: Village Nucleation
village_nucleation.observation: Scattered farmsteads are gathered into one village around shrine, manor and green, with open fields all round.
village_nucleation.ability_reason: The open fields can now be worked in common, and one priest, smith and miller serve the whole village.
village_nucleation.social_consequence: Those who would not move lose their rights in the common fields, and the manor gate becomes the village's centre.

foreign_merchant_quarters.name: Merchant Quarters
foreign_merchant_quarters.observation: Foreign merchants live in a walled quarter under their own headman, and the ships that bring their goods bring strange fevers.

single_heir_holdings.name: Undivided Farms
single_heir_holdings.observation: One heir takes the farm undivided and pays the others off in coin or goods.
single_heir_holdings.social_consequence: Brothers and sisters without land become servants or wanderers, or wait long to marry.

eldest_son_succession.name: Eldest-Son Succession
eldest_son_succession.observation: The fief and its office pass whole to the eldest son.
eldest_son_succession.ability_reason: Realms no longer shatter among brothers at every death, and a succession can be known before it comes.
eldest_son_succession.social_consequence: Younger sons are left landless and restless, and fill the religious houses, the warbands and the roads.

younger_son_careers.name: Younger Sons' Careers
younger_son_careers.observation: Younger sons are sent into religious houses, to war or into trade, so the patrimony stays whole.

realm_holding_survey.name: Great Realm Survey
realm_holding_survey.observation: Commissioners record every holding, plough, household and beast in the realm in one great book.
realm_holding_survey.ability_reason: The ruler knows what the land bears and who owes it, and the survey book becomes the final word on holdings.
realm_holding_survey.social_consequence: People call it the day of reckoning; no appeal against the book is allowed.

minimum_marriage_ages.name: Minimum Marriage Ages
minimum_marriage_ages.observation: No girl may be married before a fixed age, nor a boy before his, and child brides grow rarer.

consent_marriage.name: Marriage by Consent
consent_marriage.observation: A marriage is made by the word of the two spouses, not their kin; a forced match can be undone.
consent_marriage.ability_reason: Young couples can found their own households by their own choice, and forced marriages no longer bind.
consent_marriage.social_consequence: Clans lose their hold on alliances made by marriage, and fathers rage at secret weddings.

womens_medicine_treatise.name: Women's Medicine
womens_medicine_treatise.observation: A treatise on the diseases of women and on childbirth tells how to turn a child lying wrong and stop a bleeding.

widow_third_dower.name: Widow's Third
widow_third_dower.observation: A widow keeps a third of her husband's estate for her lifetime, whatever the heir says.

legitimation_by_marriage.name: Legitimation by Marriage
legitimation_by_marriage.observation: Children born before the wedding become lawful heirs when their parents later marry.

burgess_rolls.name: Burgess Rolls
burgess_rolls.observation: The town keeps a roll of its burgesses, those born or sworn into its freedom, and only they may trade freely.

colonist_recruiting_agents.name: Colonist Recruiters
colonist_recruiting_agents.observation: Settlement agents recruit whole villages of colonists for new lands, lead them there and become their headmen.
colonist_recruiting_agents.ability_reason: The frontier is filled by contract, not by force, and each new village arrives with a headman and a charter.
colonist_recruiting_agents.social_consequence: Old settlers and new colonists quarrel over woods and water, and the agent-headman's heirs become a new petty gentry.

heiress_fief_inheritance.name: Heiresses Inherit
heiress_fief_inheritance.observation: When no son lives, a daughter inherits the fief, and her marriage is hurried and fought over.

heir_wardship.name: Heir Wardship
heir_wardship.observation: The lord keeps the wardship and marriage of underage heirs, and sells both to the highest bidder.
heir_wardship.social_consequence: Orphaned heirs are sold as wards, and guardians strip their lands before they come of age.

burgage_plot_towns.name: Planted Towns
burgage_plot_towns.observation: New towns are laid out in equal narrow house plots for incomers, each paying a fixed rent, and the backyards fill with middens.

settler_home_law.name: Settlers' Home Law
settler_home_law.observation: Colonists keep the law of the region they came from in their new villages, and appeal to its courts.

fixed_majority_ages.name: Fixed Ages of Majority
fixed_majority_ages.observation: Heirs of arms come of age at twenty-one and others younger, and guardians must hand over on the day.

noble_lineage_rolls.name: Noble Lineage Rolls
noble_lineage_rolls.observation: Heralds keep rolls of noble lineages, and only those who can prove their descent may hold certain offices or bear arms.

dynastic_vital_register.name: Ruling-House Register
dynastic_vital_register.observation: The births, marriages and deaths of the ruling house are kept in a court register, so succession is known to all.

captive_ransom_brotherhoods.name: Ransom Brotherhoods
captive_ransom_brotherhoods.observation: Charitable brotherhoods collect silver to ransom captives taken by raiders and bring them home.

foundling_wheel.name: Foundling Wheel
foundling_wheel.observation: A turning cradle in the foundling house wall lets a mother leave her child inside unseen, and fewer are left in the cold.

public_marriage_banns.name: Marriage Banns
public_marriage_banns.observation: A coming marriage is announced in public three times, so that any bar to it can be spoken.

retirement_maintenance_contracts.name: Retirement Contracts
retirement_maintenance_contracts.observation: Aged parents hand the farm to a child in return for a written keep of food, fuel and a room.

hereditary_surnames.name: Hereditary Surnames
hereditary_surnames.observation: Family names are fixed and passed from parent to child, instead of changing with each generation.
hereditary_surnames.ability_reason: A person can be found in any roll, court or contract across the generations.
hereditary_surnames.social_consequence: Clerks write every name the same way, and a family's standing and debts follow its name.

single_women_houses.name: Single Women's Houses
single_women_houses.observation: Unmarried women and widows live and work together in houses under a simple rule, spinning and nursing for their keep.

decimal_unit_census.name: Decimal Census
decimal_unit_census.observation: Conquered lands are counted in tens, hundreds and thousands of households, each unit owing men and tribute.

holding_fragmentation.name: Divided Holdings
holding_fragmentation.observation: Holdings are split into half and quarter farms as numbers press on the land, and cottagers crowd the waste.
holding_fragmentation.social_consequence: Half-farms and cottars' plots crowd the parish, and a bad harvest now hits a people with no margin.

town_migration_dependence.name: Towns Fed by Migrants
town_migration_dependence.observation: Burials in the towns outrun baptisms year after year, and only the stream of incomers keeps the streets full.
town_migration_dependence.social_consequence: Country folk come to the towns to work and die of town fevers; the countryside pays for the town's growth in children.

purchased_corrodies.name: Corrodies
purchased_corrodies.observation: Buyers pay a religious house a lump sum for bed, board and care for the rest of their lives.

orphan_chambers.name: Orphan Chambers
orphan_chambers.observation: A town chamber keeps the property of fatherless children until they come of age, and audits the guardians.

age_priced_life_annuities.name: Life Annuities
age_priced_life_annuities.observation: Towns sell life annuities, charging an old buyer less than a young one for the same yearly payment.

entailed_family_land.name: Entailed Land
entailed_family_land.observation: Land is bound to the family line and cannot be sold or split, whatever the present holder's debts.

service_before_marriage.name: Service Before Marriage
service_before_marriage.observation: Young people spend years in service in other households and marry only when they can set up house for themselves.
service_before_marriage.ability_reason: Fewer and later births in households that can feed them: mothers are older and stronger, and more children live.
service_before_marriage.social_consequence: Servants live under a master's roof and rule, and a couple who cannot set up house must wait.

widow_trade_continuation.name: Widows Keep the Trade
widow_trade_continuation.observation: A widow may carry on her late husband's trade and shop, with his journeymen, as a guild member.

poor_bride_dowries.name: Poor Brides' Dowries
poor_bride_dowries.observation: Charitable funds give dowries to poor girls so that they can marry.

vagrant_expulsion.name: Vagrant Expulsion
vagrant_expulsion.observation: Towns whip and expel beggars and vagrants born elsewhere, and the beadle walks them to the boundary.
vagrant_expulsion.social_consequence: The landless poor are driven from town to town, and each parish passes its paupers to the next.

bread_mouth_census.name: Bread Census
bread_mouth_census.observation: In siege or dearth, officials count the mouths in every house so the bread can be rationed fairly.

sworn_town_midwives.name: Sworn Midwives
sworn_town_midwives.observation: The town swears in and licenses its midwives, who must call a second midwife to a hard birth.

deserted_village_pasture.name: Deserted Villages to Pasture
deserted_village_pasture.observation: Villages emptied by the great mortality are turned over to sheep, and the house platforms show under the grass.
deserted_village_pasture.social_consequence: Survivors are moved off or left alone amid empty holdings, and the parish church stands in a field.

adult_poll_rolls.name: Poll-Tax Rolls
adult_poll_rolls.observation: Every adult over fourteen is written in the poll roll, and the tax is laid on heads, not hearths.
adult_poll_rolls.ability_reason: The state knows how many live in the realm and can tax every adult, not only every household.
adult_poll_rolls.social_consequence: Collectors come door to door; families hide daughters and servants, and a hard poll can bring the countryside to revolt.
